workflows.name: Keys That Work Almost Anywhere
workflows.description: The fallback set, shown on a desktop this build has no specific workflows for. These four are conventional across X11 desktops rather than guaranteed — if one does nothing here, your desktop has bound it to something else.

steps.heading: Switch between windows
steps.description: Hold Alt and press Tab to walk the list of open windows. The oldest keyboard shortcut on the desktop, and the one that is bound everywhere.

steps.heading: Open a terminal
steps.description: The convention on GNOME, Cinnamon, MATE and most Ubuntu-derived desktops. Some desktops leave it unbound — if nothing opens, yours is one of them.

steps.heading: Run a command
steps.description: Opens a small box that runs a single command, without a terminal window hanging around afterwards.

steps.heading: Move to the next workspace
steps.description: Workspaces are separate screens' worth of windows. This steps to the one on the right; the left arrow comes back.
